summary: Not for buying the dip or shorting a breakdown: after every lower-band setting, price did the same as random on 1h, 4h and daily. What beat random was price above the upper band, mostly in uptrends. These candles fire in volatile stretches of a window that rose, so price moved more after them; the band did not pick direction.

verdicts.text: Same as random on 1h, 4h and daily. That held whether price crossed back up through the lower band, with Range length 10 or 20, or sat below it.

verdicts.text: Same as random on 1h, 4h and daily. After the break, price did not fall more than it did after a random candle.
Beat random on 1h, 4h and daily, almost all of it in uptrends. These candles are volatile and the window rose, so price moved more after them; that is timing, not a pick of direction.
Beat random only because of signals between Nov 5 and Nov 7, 2020. Without them it was the same as random, and like the other upper-band longs it fires in volatile candles.

notes: On 4h, buying as price crossed back up through the lower band gave 724 entries in 365 separate moves. Twenty candles later they were 0.62% behind random entries, inside the luck band. Holding below the band enters nearly three times as often and lands in the same place. A Range length of 20 does too. On 1h and daily the lower band showed the same: price did no better than after a random candle.

Going long while price was above the upper band on 4h beat random entries by 1.17% after 20 candles. It held without its strongest stretch, between Jan 30 and Feb 12, 2021, and at 10, 20, 50 and 100 candles. On daily, the cross up through the upper band beat random by about 8.5% after 20 days. Both settings fire mostly in volatile candles, and the window rose overall. So the gap shows that price moved more after them, not that the band picks direction.

The gap came from uptrends. On 4h, above the upper band beat random by 1.11% while the pair closed above its 200-day SMA. Below it, the result was 0.6%, inside the luck band and the same as random. The 4h cross up through the upper band split the same way. On daily, the uptrend result for above the upper band rests on signals between Jul 31 and Sep 9, 2021. Downtrends gave too few separate moves to judge either daily setting.

Single stretches can fake a result. On 1h, the cross up through the upper band beat random by 0.18%, but only because of signals between Nov 5 and Nov 7, 2020. Without them, and at 10 candles, it was the same as random. On ETH 4h, holding below the lower band looked 1.22% worse than random, but only because of signals between Jun 10 and Jun 18, 2022, when Celsius froze withdrawals.

For a long DCA bot, a lower-band start condition did no better than a random start on these pairs, so the DCA orders and take profit do the work. A short bot that opens on a break below the lower band also matched random, which is a reason to leave that setting out. Price above the upper band on 4h fits better as a filter beside a trend condition, such as price above the 200-day SMA. It marks volatile candles in a rising window, and in downtrends it showed nothing. Set the take profit and DCA so the bot still works if the larger move never comes.
